subject: PivHealth Dedicated Bridge & Quiesce Plan — sizing validation and cutover windows
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Lane <avery.lane@pivhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: PivHealth Dedicated Bridge & Quiesce Plan — sizing validation and cutover windows

Avery — thanks again for the time this morning. Per our call, I pulled together a compact plan so we can align the sizing validation and pick a short quiesce window for the hosted->dedicated swap. Key items below and an ask at the end. I attached the capacity matrix we used in sizing (pivotal_capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx).

High-level summary:
- Objective: move PivHealth production traffic from Hosted API to a Reserved Dedicated pool with predictable throughput and lower per-token unit cost.
- Commitment: initial reserved vGPU footprint ~40 A100-80GB equivalent (see matrix) with a 10% buffer for steady-state.
- Risk areas: peak M-F morning bursts (08:30–10:30 PT), long tail batch reranks overnight, and KV cache warmup during cutover.

Proposed validation cadence (week leading up to swap):
1) Day -7: Mirror production sampling (10% traffic) to a staging dedicated pool for throughput and latency baselining.
2) Day -4: Full traffic replay with synthetic bursts to validate autoscaling triggers and batching effects.
3) Day -2: Dry-run swap (DNS and routing rehearsals; failover validation).
4) Day 0: Planned quiesce window (2 hours) for final switchover and validation.

Quiesce window options (pick one):
- Option A: Weekday early morning (Tue 06:00–08:00 PT) — minimal user activity, easier rollback but requires overnight engineering on-call.
- Option B: Weekend night (Sat 01:00–03:00 PT) — lowest traffic, longer runway for fixes, slightly longer rollback time to Monday.

Immediate asks:
- Please confirm preferred quiesce option and whether EngOps can commit to a 4-hour on-call overlap for rollback support.
- Internal: Marissa, Soojin — can you validate the buffer and suggested autoscaling thresholds in the attached matrix by EOD Thu?

Thanks — I will follow up with a brief runbook once we pick a window.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: PivHealth Dedicated Bridge & Quiesce Plan — sizing validation and cutover windows

Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:
- We prefer Option B (Saturday 01:00–03:00 PT). Lower business impact and our compliance team prefers weekend windows for change control.
- EngOps can provide a rollback on-call (Ben from EngOps will be lead) but will need 48h notice to confirm schedules.

Couple of clarifying questions from our side:
- Can you confirm expected cold-start latency impact for chat sessions immediately after swap? We track 95p latency and want regressions <10%.
- Any recommended KV pre-warm strategy to avoid increased token costs for early morning traffic?

We will route Ben (ben@integration-partner.io) into the thread for any infra/deploy specifics.

Best,
Avery
Avery Lane
Head of Product Operations, PivHealth
avery.lane@pivhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Lane <avery.lane@pivhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@integration-partner.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PivHealth Dedicated Bridge & Quiesce Plan — sizing validation and cutover windows

Ben / Avery — copied the infra lead, Connor, and our ops owners. Quick answers and an updated ask:
- Cold-starts: based on our staging benchmarks (see matrix tab 'latency_summary'), expect a transient 15–30% increase in 95p for the first 10–20 minutes if caches are cold. Practically that maps to ~120–170ms extra at 95p for the chat flow you shared. We can minimize this with a pre-warm sequence.
- KV pre-warm: recommend a two-step approach — (1) prefix warming using a sampled set of 1M frequent prefixes 2–4 hours before swap, (2) lightweight rolling warm requests immediately after swap (30m) while we monitor tail latencies. This reduces 95p impact to within your 10% SLO.

Connor — can you and Marissa validate autoscaling thresholds (target_util 60–70%, scale_up at 75%, scale_down at 45%) and confirm the staging run uses realistic burst traffic? Marissa, please add notes to the capacity sheet with any changes.

Avery — we hear the 48h notice for EngOps on-call. Suggest we lock the final date by Thu EOD so infra can confirm. Are you comfortable with the proposed pre-warm window starting Sat 22:00 PT?

— Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PivHealth Dedicated Bridge & Quiesce Plan — sizing validation and cutover windows

Karthik/Team — reviewed the matrix and added a 'safety' column to the sheet with two small changes: +8% steady buffer, and bump scale_up to 78% to reduce oscillation on short bursts. Notes in Drive (see link). Also validated staging traffic profiles — Connor ran a 2h burst sim and we saw no queueing at 75% util with 45% target.

Concise runbook items I'm proposing (to include in the final runbook PDF):
- Pre-swap (T-6h): start prefix warm (sample set), health checks to new pool.
- T-2h: full mirror sampling (10% traffic) and autoscaler watch.
- T-30m: freeze deploys, snapshot routing table, disable cross-region fallbacks.
- T0 (01:00 PT Sat): quiesce start — 2hr window. Swap route -> dedicated. Smoke check suite (10m).
- T+30m: traffic ramp to 25% for 20m; monitor 95p tail and error rate.
- T+90m: normal ramp to 100% if metrics green.
- Rollback: immediate route revert and restart caches; expected recovery ~45–60m.

I'll prepare the PDF runbook (cutover_windows_proposal_20270302.pdf) and share latest Drive link.

— Marissa
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
